level.title: Upper intermediate: debate, work, culture
goals: Argue opinions with the subjunctive mood
Write formal emails and master Y/EN pronouns
Understand idioms and build rich hypothetical stories

lessons.title: Wishes need subjunctive (je veux que…)
lessons.learn: After wishes, French switches mood: JE VEUX QUE TU VIENNES (I want you to come). For -ER verbs the subjunctive looks the same (que tu PARLES) — the magic shows in rebels: que tu SOIS (be), que tu FASSES (do), que tu AILLES (go).

grammar.title: Subjunctive after JE VEUX QUE
grammar.explain: JE VEUX QUE + subjunctive: TU VIENS (fact) → QUE TU VIENNES (wish). Stars to memorise: QUE JE SOIS (that I be), QUE J'AIE (that I have), QUE TU FASSES, QUE TU AILLES, QUE TU VIENNES.

examples.t: Je veux que vous fassiez attention.
examples.r: zhuh vuh kuh voo fah-SYEH ah-tah(n)-SYOH(n).
examples.en: I want you to pay attention.
I hope you are ready. (espérer keeps normal!)

mistakes: Saying JE VEUX QUE TU VIENS — wishes need VIENNES.
Using subjunctive after J'ESPÈRE — hope keeps the normal form.

dialogue.en: I want you to help me.
What do you want me to do?

dialogue.t: Je veux que tu parles au patron.
dialogue.r: zhuh vuh kuh tew pahrl oh pah-TROH(n).
dialogue.en: I want you to talk to the boss.
Agreed.

practice.q: Say: I want you to come
Je veux que vous ___ attention. (pay)
'What do you want me to do?' is…
Order: viennes / veux / tu / je / que
Say aloud: Je veux que tu m'aides.

quiz.q: JE VEUX QUE TU VIENNES means…
TU VIENS → QUE TU VIENNES: the switch is…

items: I want you to pay attention
What do you want me to do?
key: Je veux que vous fassiez attention

items: I want you to help me

lessons.title: News and reported speech
lessons.learn: Report what others say: IL DIT QU'IL VIENT (he says he is coming). Past: IL A DIT QU'IL EST VENU (he said he came). News verbs: INFORMER, ANNONCER, CONFIRMER.

grammar.title: Reported speech: il dit / il a dit que…
grammar.explain: IL DIT QUE + sentence (he says that…). Past: IL A DIT QUE + past (he said that…). The intro verb moves in time; QUE always stays.
grammar.pattern: il dit que + present · il a dit que + past

examples.t: Il a dit qu'il est venu.
examples.r: eel ah dee keel eh vuh-NEW.

examples.en: The paper says it is raining.

mistakes: Forgetting QUE: IL DIT QU'il vient, with QUE!
Saying IL DIT QU'IL VIENDRAIT for simple reports — keep it simple.

dialogue.en: What does the paper say?
It says a storm is coming.

dialogue.t: Il a dit que c'est grave?
dialogue.r: eel ah dee kuh seh grahv?
dialogue.en: Did it say it is serious?

dialogue.t: Non, il a dit que c'est léger.
dialogue.r: noh(n), eel ah dee kuh seh leh-ZHEH.
dialogue.en: No, it said it is mild.

practice.q: Say: He says he is coming
Il a dit qu'il est ___ (come)
'The paper says it is raining' is…
options: Le journal a dit qu'il pleut

practice.q: Order: vient / dit / qu il / il
Say aloud: Il dit qu'une tempête arrive.

quiz.q: IL A DIT QU'IL EST VENU means…

quiz.why: Dit QUE, a dit QUE — QUE stays.

key: Il a dit qu'il est venu

items: It says a storm is coming

lessons.title: Polite professional French (conditionnel)
lessons.learn: Sound professional: J'AIMERAIS (I would like), POURRIEZ-VOUS (could you…?). Conditionnel adds imparfait endings to the future stem: PARLER → PARLERAIS. POURRIEZ-VOUS M'AIDER? = Could you help me?

grammar.title: Conditionnel: future stem + ais/iez
grammar.explain: J'AIMERAIS (I would like), VOUS POURRIEZ (you could), CE SERAIT (it would be). Same stem as future + soft -AIS/-IEZ endings. J'AIMERAIS + verb = I would like to…
mistakes: Saying J'AIME for formal wishes — J'AIMERAIS is softer.
Cutting the stem: PARLERAIS keeps -ER + AIS.

dialogue.en: Good morning, I would like to speak to Léa.
Could you tell me your name?

dialogue.t: Je suis Théo. Demain serait possible?
dialogue.r: zhuh swee teh-OH. duh-ma(n) suh-REH poh-SEEBL?
dialogue.en: I am Théo. Would tomorrow be possible?
Yes, kind regards. (closing)

practice.q: Say: I would like to speak
___ m'aider? (could you)
'Would tomorrow be possible?' is…
Order: parler / j'aimerais
Say aloud: Pourriez-vous m'aider?

items: Good morning, I would like to speak to Léa
Could you tell me your name?

lessons.title: Y and EN (little giants)
lessons.learn: Two tiny words replace whole phrases! Y = there / à + thing: J'Y VAIS (I go there). EN = some / of it: J'EN VEUX (I want some). They jump BEFORE the verb, just like LE/LA.

grammar.title: Y = there · EN = some/of it
grammar.explain: J'Y VAIS = I go (there). J'Y PENSE = I think about it. J'EN VEUX = I want some (of them). J'EN AI DEUX = I have two (of them). Before the verb — always!
mistakes: Saying JE VAIS Y — Y jumps before: J'Y VAIS.
Saying JE VEUX EN — EN jumps before: J'EN VEUX.

dialogue.en: Are you going to the party?
Yes, I go there with you.
Do you want some gifts?
Yes, I want two (of them)!

practice.q: Say: I go there tomorrow
J'en veux ___ (two)
'I want some' is…
Order: vais / j'y / demain
Say aloud: J'y vais avec toi.

quiz.q: IL Y EN A TROIS means…

items: Il y a trois cadeaux → … (of them)
Are you going to the party?

lessons.title: Idioms and sayings
lessons.learn: Idioms never translate word-for-word! POSER UN LAPIN = to stand someone up (to put a rabbit!). Learn them as whole chunks — they make you sound truly French.

vocab.t: coûter les yeux de la tête
vocab.r: koo-TEH leh zyuh duh lah tet

vocab.en: to have your head in the clouds

vocab.t: mettre les pieds dans le plat
vocab.r: metr leh pyeh dah(n) luh plah
vocab.en: to put your foot in it

grammar.title: Idioms = whole chunks, never word-for-word
grammar.explain: ÇA M'A COÛTÉ LES YEUX = it cost me a fortune (not eye shopping!). Translate the MEANING. Use idioms whole and fixed — no swapping words!

examples.en: The exam was a piece of cake.

examples.t: J'ai mis les pieds dans le plat.
examples.r: zheh mee leh pyeh dah(n) luh plah.
examples.en: I put my foot in it.

mistakes: Translating idioms literally — learn the real meaning.
Changing idiom words: POSER UN LAPIN is fixed!

dialogue.en: How was the exam?

dialogue.t: Du gâteau. J'ai fait la grasse matinée après.
dialogue.r: dew gah-TOH. zheh feh lah grahs mah-tee-NEH ah-PREH.
dialogue.en: Piece of cake. I slept in after.

dialogue.t: Tu me poses un lapin, là!
dialogue.r: tew muh pohz uhn lah-PA(n), lah!
dialogue.en: You are kidding me! (standing me up here!)
No, it's true.

practice.q: Say: The exam was a piece of cake
Il m'a posé un ___ (rabbit = stood me up)
'I feel blue' is…
Order: plat / mis / dans / le / les / pieds / j'ai
practice.answer: j'ai mis les pieds dans le plat

practice.q: Say aloud: L'examen, c'était du gâteau.

lessons.title: If-plans: s'il pleut, je reste
lessons.learn: Real plans: SI + present, + present/future. S'IL PLEUT, JE RESTE (if it rains, I stay). SI TU VIENS, JE T'AIDE (if you come, I help you). Cause meets result — never future after SI!

grammar.title: Real SI: si + present, + result
grammar.explain: S'IL PLEUT (if it rains) → JE RESTE (I stay). Both verbs present, or result in future: SI TU VIENS, JE T'AIDERAI. Real, possible plans only — and NEVER future right after SI!

examples.en: If you come, I help you.
If you study, you will pass.

mistakes: Using future after SI: S'IL PLEUT (present!), never S'IL PLEUVRA.
Forgetting the comma pause between condition and result.

dialogue.en: If it rains, what do we do?

dialogue.t: S'il pleut, je reste à la maison.
dialogue.r: seel pluh, zhuh rest ah lah meh-ZOH(n).
dialogue.en: If it rains, I stay home.

dialogue.t: Et s'il fait beau, on va à la plage.
dialogue.r: eh seel feh boh, oh(n) vah ah lah plahzh.
dialogue.en: And if it is sunny, we go to the beach.
Good decision!

practice.q: Say: If it rains, I stay
Si tu ___, je t'aide. (come)
'If you study, you will pass' is…
Order: reste / pleut / s'il / je
Say aloud: S'il pleut, je reste.

quiz.q: SI TU ÉTUDIES, TU RÉUSSIRAS: the result verb is…
